correspondences.note_fr: L'article 128 énumère diverses conventions de mise en état, notamment sur la limitation du débat, les échanges, les techniciens et la consignation des auditions et témoignages. Les règles du Missouri couvrent séparément la gestion de l'instance, la discovery, les dépositions et la production de documents, mais sans organiser ce régime conventionnel global.
correspondences.note_en: Article 128 lists party agreements concerning issues, exchanges, experts, examinations, and witness statements. The Missouri provisions separately address case management, discovery, depositions, and document production, but do not create the same comprehensive contractual case-preparation framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 160 règle la convocation des parties et des tiers à l’exécution d’une mesure d’instruction, notamment par lettre recommandée, bulletin remis au défenseur ou convocation verbale. Les Rules 57.03 et 57.09 organisent respectivement l’avis de déposition et la citation des témoins, mais dans le cadre plus spécifique des dépositions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 160 governs summoning parties and non-parties to participate in an evidentiary measure, including by registered letter, notice through counsel, or oral notice. Rules 57.03 and 57.09 regulate deposition notices and subpoenas, but only within the more specific deposition framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 161 autorise les parties à se faire assister pendant la mesure et à ne pas y assister lorsque leur audition personnelle n’est pas nécessaire. La Rule 57.03 permet la participation des avocats aux dépositions, notamment à distance, mais ne reprend pas exactement la faculté générale de dispense de présence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 161 permits parties to be assisted during an evidentiary measure and to dispense with attendance when personal examination is unnecessary. Rule 57.03 permits attorneys to participate in depositions, including remotely, but does not reproduce the general right to forgo attendance.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 162 permet au représentant ou à l’assistant d’une partie de suivre l’exécution de la mesure, de présenter des observations et des demandes, même en l’absence de la partie. Les Rules 57.03 et 57.07 reconnaissent la participation des avocats et encadrent leurs objections pendant les dépositions, sans reprendre l’ensemble de ces pouvoirs.
correspondences.note_en: Article 162 allows a party’s representative or attorney to attend the measure, make observations, and present related requests even without the party. Rules 57.03 and 57.07 provide for attorney participation and objections during depositions, but do not confer all of these powers expressly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 191 impose des réponses personnelles aux questions, sans lecture d’un projet. La Rule 57.03 prévoit l’interrogatoire oral d’un témoin ou d’une partie, mais le texte fourni ne contient pas l’interdiction de lire un projet ni une exigence équivalente de réponse personnelle.
correspondences.note_en: Article 191 requires parties to answer questions personally and without reading from a draft. Rule 57.03 governs oral examination of a witness or party, but the supplied text contains no prohibition on reading a draft or equivalent personal-answer requirement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 192 exige la comparution personnelle en présence des défenseurs de toutes les parties, ou après leur convocation. La Rule 57.03 impose un préavis de sept jours à toutes les autres parties et permet la participation des avocats, notamment à distance, mais n’exige pas leur présence effective.
correspondences.note_en: Article 192 requires personal appearance in the presence of all parties’ counsel, or after counsel have been called. Rule 57.03 requires seven days’ notice to every other party and permits attorneys to participate, including remotely, but does not require their actual attendance.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 57.03 prévoit l’enregistrement ou la transcription du témoignage lors d’une déposition, mais ne règle ni l’absence ou le refus de répondre des parties ni la possibilité de remplacer le procès-verbal par une mention au jugement.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 57.03 provides for recording or transcription of deposition testimony, but does not address a party’s absence or refusal to answer, or replacement of the record by a judgment notation.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut entendre les mineurs, majeurs protégés, représentants de personnes morales et agents ou membres de celles-ci. La Rule 57.03(b)(4) prévoit la désignation de représentants d’une organisation pour une déposition, tandis que la Rule 52.02 et le RSMo 510.020 concernent respectivement la représentation des personnes vulnérables et l’interrogatoire des parties ou sociétés.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may examine minors, protected adults, representatives of legal entities, and their members or agents. Rule 57.03(b)(4) provides for organizational representatives to testify by deposition, while Rule 52.02 and RSMo 510.020 address representation of vulnerable persons and interrogatories to parties or entities.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 203 permet au juge d’entendre lui-même, par voie d’enquête, l’auteur d’une attestation. La Rule 57.03 permet de recueillir par deposition orale le témoignage de toute personne, mais à l’initiative d’une partie et sans viser spécifiquement l’auteur d’une attestation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 203 allows the judge to examine the author of a written attestation through an evidentiary inquiry. Rule 57.03 permits a party to obtain any person’s testimony by oral deposition, serving a comparable fact-gathering function but through a different mechanism and without the judge-initiated authority provided by the CPC.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe largement l’aptitude à témoigner, prévoit l’audition sans serment de certaines personnes et exclut les descendants dans certains litiges matrimoniaux. Rule 57.03 et RSMo 210.839 offrent seulement des parallèles limités sur l’audition et la compétence; aucune disposition retenue ne traite des deux dernières règles françaises.
correspondences.note_en: The article broadly governs witness eligibility, unsworn testimony by certain persons, and exclusion of descendants in specified matrimonial disputes. Rule 57.03 and RSMo 210.839 provide only limited parallels concerning testimony and competency; neither addresses the latter two French rules.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la déposition lorsqu’elle est légalement requise, tout en prévoyant des motifs légitimes d’exemption et des refus fondés sur certains liens familiaux. Rule 57.09 organise la subpoena et le contempt; Rule 57.03 et RSMo 210.832 prévoient la contrainte, mais sans reprendre l’ensemble des exemptions françaises.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires testimony when lawfully compelled, while recognizing legitimate excuses and refusals based on specified family relationships. Rule 57.09 governs subpoenas and contempt; Rule 57.03 and RSMo 210.832 provide compulsion, but do not reproduce all of the French exemptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L'enquête doit se dérouler en présence des défenseurs de toutes les parties ou après convocation. La Rule 57.03(b)(1) impose une notification écrite à toutes les parties, tandis que la Rule 57.07 reconnaît l'utilisation de la déposition lorsque la partie était présente, représentée ou régulièrement avisée; ces règles ne garantissent pas exactement la présence effective.
correspondences.note_en: The inquiry must occur with all parties’ counsel present or called. Rule 57.03(b)(1) requires written notice to every party, and Rule 57.07 permits use of a deposition when a party was present, represented, or properly notified; these provisions do not exactly require actual attendance.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au témoin de décliner son identité complète, sa profession et ses liens avec les parties. La Rule 57.03 exige l’identification du déposant dans l’avis de déposition, mais ne prévoit ni cette déclaration générale ni l’ensemble des renseignements requis.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a witness to provide complete identifying details, occupation, and relationships with the parties. Rule 57.03 requires the deponent to be identified in a deposition notice, but does not impose the same general disclosure or require all of these particulars.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose le serment de dire la vérité, l’information sur les sanctions du faux témoignage et, pour les personnes non assermentées, l’information de leur obligation de vérité. Les règles du Missouri prévoient la prestation du serment ou d’une affirmation, mais pas l’ensemble de ces avertissements ni le régime spécifique des personnes non assermentées.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an oath to tell the truth, a warning about false-testimony penalties, and notice of the truth obligation for unsworn persons. The Missouri rules provide for an oath or affirmation, but not all of these warnings or the specific treatment of unsworn persons.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 57.03 concerne les dépositions : elle prévoit la consignation des objections relatives à la conduite et permet une sanction en cas d’entrave à l’examen. Elle ne reprend pas l’interdiction française de s’adresser directement aux témoins ni le pouvoir du juge de poser les questions des parties.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 57.03 concerns depositions: it provides for recording objections regarding conduct and permits sanctions for impeding the examination. It does not reproduce the French prohibition on directly addressing witnesses or the judge’s power to ask the parties’ questions.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut réentendre les témoins, les confronter entre eux ou avec les parties, éventuellement en présence d’un technicien. La Rule 57.03 permet, sous conditions, une nouvelle déposition ; la Rule 68.01 permet au master de conduire une audition et d’examiner les témoins, sans prévoir expressément la confrontation ni l’assistance d’un technicien.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may hear witnesses again, confront them with one another or with the parties, and, where appropriate, conduct the hearing with a technician present. Rule 57.03 permits a further deposition subject to conditions, and Rule 68.01 permits a master to conduct hearings and examine witnesses, but neither expressly provides for confrontation or a technician.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet de reporter l’audition d’un témoin empêché de se déplacer ou au juge de se transporter pour recueillir sa déposition. La Rule 57.03 autorise notamment les dépositions à distance, la Rule 65.04 encadre le report pour absence d’un témoin, et la Rule 57.09 permet de contraindre sa présence, sans prévoir exactement le déplacement du juge.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits postponing the examination of a witness unable to travel or having the judge travel to take the testimony. Rule 57.03 allows, among other things, remote depositions; Rule 65.04 governs continuances for an absent witness; and Rule 57.09 compels attendance, but none exactly provides for the judge’s travel.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la consignation des dépositions dans un procès-verbal et prévoit une exception lorsque les témoignages sont recueillis aux débats. Les Rules 57.03 et 57.04 organisent l’enregistrement, la transcription et la certification des dépositions, mais ne reprennent pas exactement cette exception liée au jugement immédiat.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires depositions to be recorded in an official report, with an exception when testimony is taken during the hearing and the case is immediately decided. Rules 57.03 and 57.04 govern recording, transcription, and certification of depositions, but do not reproduce that specific exception.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article détaille le contenu, la signature, les observations et les annexes du procès-verbal d’enquête. Les Rules 57.03 et 57.04 prévoient l’enregistrement et la certification des dépositions; Rule 68.01 et RSMo 513.390 prévoient la conservation écrite des témoignages, mais aucun texte ne reprend l’ensemble des formalités CPC.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies the contents, signatures, observations, and attachments required for the examination record. Rules 57.03 and 57.04 address recording and certification; Rule 68.01 and RSMo 513.390 provide for written records of testimony, but none reproduces all of the CPC formalities.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose à la partie qui sollicite une enquête, ainsi qu’à la décision qui l’ordonne, d’identifier les témoins par leurs nom, prénoms et domicile. La Rule 57.03(b)(1) exige le nom et l’adresse du déposant, avec une description si le nom est inconnu, tandis que la Rule 57.02 exige l’identification des personnes à entendre dans une procédure de conservation de témoignage.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the requesting party and the order directing the inquiry to identify witnesses by name and residence. Rule 57.03(b)(1) requires the deponent’s name and address, allowing a description if unknown, while Rule 57.02 requires identification of persons to be examined in a testimony-preservation proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet une désignation différée ou une présentation directe de témoins lorsque leur identité ne peut être indiquée d’emblée, y compris dans une enquête ordonnée d’office. La Rule 57.03(b)(1) admet une description lorsque le nom est inconnu, et la Rule 57.02 permet à l’ordonnance de désigner ou décrire les personnes à entendre, mais dans des procédures de déposition distinctes.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits deferred identification or direct production of witnesses when their identities cannot initially be supplied, including in a court-ordered inquiry. Rule 57.03(b)(1) permits a sufficient description when the name is unknown, and Rule 57.02 permits an order designating or describing persons to be examined, but in different deposition proceedings.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1974 This is substantially the same as Rule 27 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 242 autorise le technicien à recueillir des renseignements auprès de toute personne, sous réserve de l’identification de celle-ci, et prévoit une audition judiciaire éventuelle. La Rule 57.03 organise la déposition de toute personne, tandis que la Rule 56.01 vise l’identification des personnes informées; ces mécanismes sont plus formels et ne confèrent pas ce pouvoir général au technicien.
correspondences.note_en: Article 242 allows a court-appointed technician to obtain information from any person, subject to identifying details, and permits a judicial hearing if useful. Rule 57.03 provides formal depositions of any person, while Rule 56.01 addresses identifying persons with discoverable knowledge; neither grants the same general power to a technician.

correspondences.note_fr: Peuvent témoigner ceux qui ont vu écrire ou signer l'acte, ainsi que toute personne utile à la vérité. Rule 57.03 permet de recueillir par déposition le témoignage de toute personne, Rule 57.09 d'en contraindre la présence, et Rule 56.01 d'identifier les personnes détenant des informations pertinentes.
correspondences.note_en: Persons who saw the writing or signature, and others useful to the truth, may testify. Rule 57.03 permits testimony by deposition, Rule 57.09 can compel attendance, and Rule 56.01 permits discovery of persons having relevant knowledge, but none reproduces the handwriting-verification rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet à une partie de déférer le serment et charge le juge d’en vérifier l’admissibilité et la pertinence des faits. La Rule 68.03 et les RSMo 210.832 et Rule 57.03 organisent respectivement l’examen sous serment, la contrainte de témoignage pertinent ou la déposition, mais sans reprendre le mécanisme général du serment décisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article lets a party refer an oath and requires the judge to assess admissibility and select relevant facts. Rule 68.03, RSMo 210.832, and Rule 57.03 provide for sworn examination, compelled testimony on relevant facts, or depositions, but do not reproduce the general decisive-oath mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 57.03 prévoit le serment et l’avis de déposition, la Rule 43.01 la transmission des ordres au représentant ou à la partie, et le RSMo 515.150 une sanction en cas de refus de prêter serment ou de répondre. Ces textes ne prévoient ni l’avertissement pénal ni le régime français du serment décisoire.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 57.03 provides for the oath and deposition notice, Rule 43.01 for transmitting orders to counsel or a party, and RSMo 515.150 for refusal to be sworn or answer. These provisions do not provide the criminal warning or the French decisive-oath regime.

correspondences.note_fr: Après l’exécution, le greffe transmet à la juridiction commettante les procès-verbaux ainsi que les pièces et objets annexés ou déposés. La Rule 57.03 prévoit l’enregistrement et, sur demande, la transcription du témoignage, mais ne règle pas sa transmission par un greffe à une autre juridiction.
correspondences.note_en: After completion, the executing clerk sends the minutes and attached or deposited materials to the referring court. Rule 57.03 addresses recording and, on request, transcription of deposition testimony, but does not provide for clerk-to-court transmission.

correspondences.note_fr: L’exécution suit en principe la loi française, sauf forme particulière demandée, avec transcription ou enregistrement intégral sur demande. Rule 57.08 prend en compte le droit étranger, tandis que Rules 57.05 et 57.03 prévoient lettres rogatoires et modalités d’enregistrement, mais avec des effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: Execution generally follows French law unless a particular form is requested, with complete transcription or recording on request. Rule 57.08 gives regard to foreign law, while Rules 57.05 and 57.03 address letters rogatory and recording, but with materially different effects.

correspondences.note_fr: Les parties et leurs défenseurs peuvent poser des questions avec l’autorisation du juge, lesquelles doivent être en français, comme les réponses. Rule 57.03 concerne l’interrogatoire oral et la participation des avocats, mais ne prévoit ni cette autorisation ni l’exigence linguistique.
correspondences.note_en: Parties and counsel may ask questions with judicial authorization, and both questions and answers must be in French. Rule 57.03 concerns oral depositions and attorney participation, but does not provide the same authorization requirement or language rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 747-1 permet, avec autorisation du ministère de la justice, l'audition directe par la juridiction étrangère, notamment par visioconférence, sans contrainte ni sanction. La règle 57.08 organise l'aide du tribunal du lieu du déposant, tandis que les règles 57.05 et 57.03 prévoient d'autres modalités de déposition et de visioconférence, généralement avec possibilité de subpoena.
correspondences.note_en: Article 747-1 permits, with Ministry of Justice authorization, a foreign court to conduct a hearing directly, including by videoconference, without compulsion or sanctions. Rule 57.08 provides court assistance where the deponent is found, while Rules 57.05 and 57.03 address other deposition and videoconference methods, generally with subpoena availability.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’instruction arbitrale, l’audition de personnes et la production forcée de pièces sous astreinte. Les Rules 56.01, 58.01 et 57.03 offrent des mécanismes judiciaires comparables de découverte, de production et de déposition; la Rule 61.01 prévoit des sanctions, mais dans un cadre et selon des effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs arbitral investigation, witness hearing, and compelled production subject to a coercive penalty. Rules 56.01, 58.01, and 57.03 provide comparable court-discovery, production, and deposition mechanisms; Rule 61.01 supplies enforcement sanctions, but in a different setting and with different effects.

norms.heading: Depositions Upon Written Questions

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 57 — Interrogatories and Depositions

norms.text:
(a) Serving Questions; Notice.

(1) After commencement of the action, any party may take the testimony of any person, including a party, by deposition upon written questions, without leave of court, except as specified in paragraph (2) of this subdivision. The attendance of witnesses may be compelled by the use of subpoena as provided in Rule 57.09.
(2) Leave of court, granted with or without notice, must be obtained only if:

(A) the parties have not stipulated to the deposition and:

(i) the deposition would result in more than 10 depositions being taken under this Rule or Rule 57.03 by the plaintiffs, or by the defendants, or by the third-party defendants;
(ii) the deponent has already been deposed in the case; or

(iii) the plaintiff seeks to take a deposition prior to the expiration of 30 days after service of the summons and petition upon any defendant, except that leave is not required if a defendant has served a notice of taking deposition or otherwise sought discovery; or
(B) the deponent is confined in prison.
(3) A party desiring to take a deposition upon written questions shall serve them upon every other party with a notice stating: (A) the name and address of the person who is to answer them, if known, and if the name is not known, a general description sufficient to identify the person or the particular class or group to which the person belongs and (B) the name or descriptive title and address of the officer before whom the deposition is to be taken.
A deposition upon written questions may be taken of a public or private corporation or a partnership or association or governmental agency in accordance with the provisions of Rule 57.03(b)(4).

(4) Within 30 days after the notice and written questions are served, a party may serve cross questions upon all other parties. Within 10 days after being served with cross questions, a party may serve redirect questions upon all other parties. Within 10 days after being served with redirect questions, a party may serve recross questions upon all other parties. The court may for cause shown enlarge or shorten the time.
(b) Officer to Take Responses and Prepare Record. A copy of the notice and copies of all questions served shall be delivered by the party taking the deposition to the officer designated in the notice, who shall proceed promptly, in the manner provided by Rule 57.03(d), (f), and (g), to take the testimony of the witness in response to the questions and to prepare, certify, and deliver the deposition, attaching thereto the copy of the notice and the questions.
(c) Notice of Delivery. When the deposition is delivered, the party taking it promptly shall give notice thereof of all other parties.

norms.heading: Persons Before Whom Depositions May Be Taken

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 57 — Interrogatories and Depositions

norms.text:
(a) In Missouri. Within the State of Missouri, depositions shall be taken before an officer authorized by the laws of this State to administer oaths, or before a person appointed by the court in which the action is pending. A person so appointed has power to administer oaths and take testimony.
(b) Elsewhere in the United States. Within other States of the United States or within a territory or insular possession subject to the dominion of the United States, depositions shall be taken before a person authorized to administer oaths by the laws of the United States or of the place where the examination is held, or before a person appointed by the court in which the action is pending. A person so appointed has power to administer oaths and take testimony.
(c) In Foreign Countries. In a foreign country, a deposition may be taken:

(1) On notice before a person authorized to administer oaths in the place in which the examination is held, either by the law thereof or by the law of the United States, or

(2) Before a person commissioned by the court, and a person so commissioned has the power by virtue of his commission to administer any necessary oath and take testimony, or
(3) Pursuant to a letter rogatory. A commission or a letter rogatory shall be issued on application and notice and on terms that are just and appropriate. It is not requisite to the issuance of a commission or a letter rogatory that the taking of the deposition in any other manner is impracticable or inconvenient; and both a commission and a letter rogatory may be issued in proper cases.
A notice or commission may designate the person before whom the deposition is to be taken either by name or descriptive title. A letter rogatory may be addressed 'To the Appropriate Authority in [here name the country]'. Evidence obtained in response to a letter rogatory need not be excluded merely for the reason that it is not a verbatim transcript or that the testimony was not taken under oath or for any similar departure from the requirements for depositions taken within the United States under these Rules.
(d) Disqualification for Interest. No deposition shall be taken before a person who is a relative or employee or attorney or counsel of any of the parties, or is a relative or employee of such attorney or counsel, or is financially interested in the action.

norms.heading: Use of Depositions in Court Proceedings

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 57 — Interrogatories and Depositions

norms.text:
(a) Use of Depositions. Any part of a deposition that is admissible under the rules of evidence applied as though the deponent were testifying in court may be used against any party who was present or represented at the taking of the deposition or who had proper notice thereof. Depositions may be used in court for any purpose.
(b) Objections – Effect of Errors and Irregularities in Depositions.

(1) Regarding the Notice. An objection to an irregularity in a deposition notice shall be made promptly by written notice served on all parties before the deposition starts; otherwise, the objection is waived.

(2) Regarding the Officer. An objection to a deposition because the officer before whom it is to be taken is not qualified shall be made before the deposition begins or as soon thereafter as the officer's lack of qualification becomes known or could have been discovered with reasonable diligence; otherwise, the objection is waived.
(3) Regarding the Competency of the Deponent. An objection to a deponent's competency is not waived by failing to make an objection before or during the deposition unless the basis for the objection could have been removed if the objection had been presented before or during the deposition.
(4) Regarding Conduct During the Deposition. An objection to the competency, relevancy, or materiality of testimony is not waived by failure to object before or during the deposition. Errors and irregularities in the manner of taking the deposition, in the form of the questions or answers, in the oath or affirmation, or in the conduct of parties and errors of any kind that might be cured if promptly presented are waived unless seasonable objection thereto is made during the deposition.
Objections as to the form of written questions submitted under Rule 57.04 are waived unless served in writing upon the party propounding them within the time allowed for serving the succeeding cross or other questions and within ten days after service of the last questions authorized.
(5) Regarding Irregularities in Transcription. Errors and irregularities in the manner in which the testimony is transcribed or the deposition is prepared, signed, certified, sealed, endorsed, transmitted, filed, or otherwise dealt with by the officer under Rule 57.03 and Rule 57.04 are waived unless a motion to suppress the deposition or some party thereof is made with reasonable promptness after such defect is, or with due diligence might have been discovered.

norms.heading: Subpoena for Taking Deposition

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 57 — Interrogatories and Depositions

norms.text:
(a) For Attendance of Witnesses; Form; Issuance. Every subpoena for a deposition shall:

(1) Be issued by the officer or person before whom depositions may be taken as designated in Rule 57.05 or Rule 57.06 or by the clerk of the court in which the civil action is pending;
(2) State the name of the court and the style of the civil action;

(3) State the name, address and telephone number of all attorneys of record and self-represented parties; and

(4) Command each person to whom it is directed to attend and give testimony at a time and place therein specified.
(b) For Production of Documents and Things. In conjunction with a deposition properly noticed under Rule 57.03, a subpoena may also command the person to whom it is directed to produce the books, papers, documents, or tangible things designated therein.

The court may:

(1) Quash or modify the subpoena if it is unreasonable or oppressive, or
(2) Require the party who issued and served the subpoena to advance the reasonable cost of producing the books, papers, documents, or tangible things.

(c) Subpoena to a Non-Party. A subpoena to a non-party pursuant to Rule 57.09 for the production of documents and things shall be served not fewer than 10 days before the time specified for compliance. The party serving a subpoena on a non-party shall provide a copy of the subpoena to every party as if it were a pleading. A party objecting to the subpoena may seek a protective order under Rule 56.01(c).
A party or attorney responsible for the issuance and service of a subpoena shall take reasonable steps to avoid imposing undue burden or expense on a non-party subject to the subpoena.
With the agreement of all parties, the non-party may be excused from appearance at the deposition and may produce the subpoenaed items to the party responsible for issuance and service of the subpoena, who shall then offer to all other parties the opportunity to inspect or copy the subpoenaed items. The party responsible for issuance and service of the subpoena is responsible for obtaining the agreement of all parties and advising the non-party in writing of the agreement, with a copy to all attorneys of record and self-represented parties. Absent such an agreement, the subpoenaed items shall only be produced at the deposition.
Upon request by any party, the non-party shall also produce with the subpoenaed items a business records affidavit of the custodian of records.

A non-party commanded to produce and permit inspection and copying may serve the party who issued and served the subpoena with a written objection to inspection and copying of any or all of the designated items. The objection shall state specific reasons why the subpoena should be quashed or modified.
The objection shall be served on all parties to the action within 10 days after service of the subpoena or before the time specified for compliance, whichever is earlier.

If a timely and specific objection is made, the party who issued and served the subpoena shall not be entitled to inspect or copy the subpoenaed items except pursuant to an order of the court.
Upon notice to the non-party commanded to produce, the party who issued and served the subpoena may move at any time for an order to compel production.

(d) Service. A subpoena may be served by:

(1) The sheriff or a sheriff's deputy, or

(2) Any other person who is not a party and is not less than 18 years of age.
Service of a subpoena upon a person named therein shall be made by delivering a copy thereof to such person and by tendering to that person the fees and mileage the witness would have been entitled to receive for attending court pursuant to subpoena.

(e) Authorization to Issue Subpoena. Proof of service of a notice to take a deposition as provided in Rules 57.03 and 57.04 is sufficient to authorize the issuance of a subpoena for taking a deposition.
(f) Contempt. Any person who without adequate excuse fails to obey a subpoena served upon the person may be held in contempt of the court in which the civil action is pending.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article permet de citer à leurs frais les témoins défaillants et de les condamner à une amende civile, avec décharge possible en cas d'empêchement justifié. correspondences.note_en: The article permits defaulting witnesses to be subpoenaed at their expense and fined, with possible relief for a justified inability to appear. Rule 57.09 governs subpoenas, tender of witness fees and mileage, and contempt for failure without adequate excuse, but not this civil fine or discharge mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 228 impose une convocation des témoins par le greffier au moins huit jours avant l’enquête. La Rule 57.09 prévoit l’émission et la signification d’une subpoena ordonnant la comparution, tandis que la Rule 57.03 prévoit un préavis écrit de sept jours, mais ces règles concernent les dépositions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 228 requires the clerk to summon witnesses at least eight days before the inquiry. Rule 57.09 governs issuance and service of a subpoena compelling attendance, and Rule 57.03 requires seven days’ written notice, but both Missouri rules concern depositions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 229 exige que la convocation identifie les parties et reproduise certaines dispositions légales. La Rule 57.09 exige notamment le nom du tribunal, l’intitulé de l’action et les coordonnées des avocats ou parties non représentées ; la Rule 57.03 exige l’identification du déposant et du lieu et de la date.
correspondences.note_en: Article 229 requires the summons to identify the parties and reproduce specified statutory provisions. Rule 57.09 requires the court name, case style, and attorney or self-represented-party information; Rule 57.03 requires identification of the deponent and the deposition details, but neither reproduces the cited provisions.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut imposer à des tiers la remise de documents, sous astreinte, et prescrire des mesures de conservation, consultation, reproduction et restitution. Les règles du Missouri organisent la subpoena et la production par les non-parties, avec possibilité de contempt, mais ne détaillent pas toutes ces mesures de gestion documentaire.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may compel third parties to produce documents, under coercion, and prescribe preservation, inspection, copying, and return measures. Missouri rules provide subpoenas and production by non-parties, with possible contempt, but do not detail all of these document-management measures.

correspondences.note_fr: Peuvent témoigner ceux qui ont vu écrire ou signer l'acte, ainsi que toute personne utile à la vérité. Rule 57.03 permet de recueillir par déposition le témoignage de toute personne, Rule 57.09 d'en contraindre la présence, et Rule 56.01 d'identifier les personnes détenant des informations pertinentes.
correspondences.note_en: Persons who saw the writing or signature, and others useful to the truth, may testify. Rule 57.03 permits testimony by deposition, Rule 57.09 can compel attendance, and Rule 56.01 permits discovery of persons having relevant knowledge, but none reproduces the handwriting-verification rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 747-2 prévoit que le ministère de la justice fixe les conditions d'exécution et peut désigner le tribunal judiciaire chargé d'assister la juridiction étrangère. La règle 57.08 permet au tribunal du comté de délivrer une subpoena et de rendre les ordonnances utiles; les règles 57.09 et 57.05 complètent respectivement la contrainte et les commissions rogatoires.
correspondences.note_en: Article 747-2 provides that the Ministry of Justice sets the conditions and may designate the judicial court assisting the foreign court. Rule 57.08 allows the court where the deponent is found to issue a subpoena and make supporting orders; Rules 57.09 and 57.05 address compulsion and commissions or letters rogatory.

norms.heading: Production of Documents and Things and Entry Upon Land for Inspection and Other Purposes

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 58 — Production of Documents and Things and Entry Upon Land for Inspection and Other Purposes

norms.text:
(a) Scope. Any party may serve on any other party a request to:

(1) Produce and permit the requesting party or its representative to inspect, copy, test, or sample the following items in the responding party's possession, custody, or control:

(A) Any designated documents or electronically stored information including writings, drawings, graphs, charts, photographs, sound recordings, images, electronic records, and other data or compilations from which information can be obtained either directly or indirectly or, if necessary, after translation by the responding party into reasonably usable form; or
(B) Any designated tangible things; or

(2) Permit entry upon designated land or other property in the possession or control of the party upon whom the request is served for the purpose of inspection and measuring, surveying, and photographing, testing, or sampling the property or any designated object or operation thereon, within the scope of Rule 56.01(b).
This Rule 58.01 does not preclude an independent action against a person not a party for production of documents and things and permission to enter upon land.

(b) Issuance.

(1) Form. In consecutively numbered paragraphs the request shall:

(A) Set forth with reasonable particularity each item or category of items to be inspected;
(B) Specify a reasonable time, place, and manner of making the inspection and performing the related acts; and

(C) May specify that electronically stored information be produced in native format.

The title shall identify the party to whom the requests are directed and state the number of the set of requests directed to that party.

(2) When Requests May Be Served. Without leave of court, requests may be served on:
(A) A plaintiff after commencement of the action, and

(B) Any other party with or after the party was served with process, entered an appearance, or filed a pleading.
(3) Service. Copies of the requests shall be served on all parties not in default. The party issuing the requests shall also provide each responding party an electronic copy in a commonly used medium, such as a diskette, CD-ROM, or as an e-mail attachment, in a format that can be read by most commonly used word processing programs, such as Word for Windows or WordPerfect 5.x or higher. In addition to the information normally in a certificate of service, the certificate of service shall also state the:
(A) Name of each party who is to respond to the requests;

(B) Number of the set of requests; and

(C) Format of the electronic copy and the medium used to transmit the electronic copy to the responding party.

At the time of service, a certificate of service, but not the requests, shall be filed with the court as provided in Rule 58.01(d).
(c) Response. The requests shall be answered by each party to whom they are directed.

(1) When Response Is Due. Responses shall be served within 30 days after the service of the request. A defendant, however, shall not be required to respond to the request before the expiration of 45 days after the earlier of:
(A) The date the defendant enters an appearance; or

(B) The date the defendant is served with process.

The court may allow a shorter or longer time.

(2) Form. The title of the response shall identify the responding party and the number of the set of the requests. The response shall quote each request, including its original paragraph number, and immediately thereunder state that the requested items will be produced or the inspection and related activities will be permitted as requested, unless the request is objected to, in which event each reason for objection shall be stated in detail.
(3) Objections and Privileges. If information is withheld because of an objection, then each reason for the objection shall be stated. An objection to part of a request must specify the part and permit inspection of the rest. If a privilege or the work product doctrine is asserted as a reason for the objection, then without revealing the protected information, the objecting party shall state information that will permit others to assess the applicability of the privilege or work product doctrine.
(4) Method of Production. A party who produces documents for inspection shall produce them as they are kept in the usual course of business so long as this form is reasonably usable by the requesting party, or shall organize and label them to correspond with the categories in the request.

(5) Signing. The response shall be signed by the attorney or by the party if the party is not represented by an attorney.
(6) Service. The party to whom the requests were directed shall serve a signed original of the response and objections, if any, on the party that issued the requests and a copy upon all parties not in default. The certificate of service shall state the name of the party who issued the requests and the number of the set of requests.
At the time of service, a certificate of service, but not the response, shall be filed with the court as provided in Rule 58.01(d).
(d) Filing. The request and responses thereto shall not be filed with the court except upon court order or contemporaneously with a motion placing the request in issue. However, both when the request and responses are served, the party serving them shall file with the court a certificate of service. The certificate shall show the caption of the case, the name of the party served, the date and manner of service, and the signature of the serving party or attorney. Each party filing a certificate shall maintain a copy of the document that is the subject of the certificate until the case is finally disposed.
(e) Enforcement. The party submitting the request may move for an order under Rule 61.01(d) with respect to any objection or other failure to respond to the request or any part thereof or any failure to permit inspection as requested.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 11 impose la coopération aux mesures d’instruction, autorise la production forcée de documents détenus par une partie ou un tiers et permet des conséquences en cas de refus. Les Rules 58.01 et 58.02 organisent la production par les parties et les tiers, tandis que la Rule 61.01 prévoit les sanctions, avec des modalités distinctes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 11 requires cooperation with investigative measures, allows compelled production from parties or non-parties, and permits consequences for refusal. Rules 58.01 and 58.02 regulate production by parties and non-parties, while Rule 61.01 provides sanctions, subject to different procedures and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 128 énumère diverses conventions de mise en état, notamment sur la limitation du débat, les échanges, les techniciens et la consignation des auditions et témoignages. Les règles du Missouri couvrent séparément la gestion de l'instance, la discovery, les dépositions et la production de documents, mais sans organiser ce régime conventionnel global.
correspondences.note_en: Article 128 lists party agreements concerning issues, exchanges, experts, examinations, and witness statements. The Missouri provisions separately address case management, discovery, depositions, and document production, but do not create the same comprehensive contractual case-preparation framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article permet de demander au juge, sans forme, d'enjoindre la communication non effectuée. Le Missouri prévoit une demande de production et une motion visant à obtenir une ordonnance de contrainte, généralement avec des exigences procédurales et un préavis.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits an informal request for a judicial order compelling missing disclosure. Missouri provides document requests and motions to compel or enforce production, generally subject to specified procedural requirements and notice.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article permet au juge de fixer le délai et les modalités de communication, éventuellement sous astreinte. RSMo 510.030 prévoit que l'ordonnance précise le temps, le lieu et les modalités; les règles de discovery organisent les délais et sanctions, mais pas une astreinte équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes the judge to set the deadline and method of disclosure, potentially backed by a coercive penalty. RSMo 510.030 requires an order to specify time, place, and manner; discovery rules provide deadlines and sanctions but no equivalent astreinte.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 142 renvoie aux articles 138 et 139 pour les demandes et la production des éléments de preuve détenus par une partie. La Rule 58.01 prévoit directement les demandes de production entre parties, tandis que RSMo 510.030 organise une production ordonnée par le tribunal sur motion et pour bonne cause.
correspondences.note_en: Article 142 refers to Articles 138 and 139 for requests to produce evidence held by a party and for its production. Rule 58.01 directly governs party requests for production, while RSMo 510.030 provides for court-ordered production upon motion and a showing of good cause.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 243 permet au technicien de demander tous documents aux parties et aux tiers, le juge intervenant en cas de difficulté. La Rule 58.01 régit la production par les parties, la Rule 58.02 celle imposée aux non-parties par subpoena, et le RSMo 515.130 reconnaît un pouvoir documentaire aux referees; les procédures et titulaires du pouvoir diffèrent.
correspondences.note_en: Article 243 permits a technician to request documents from parties and non-parties, with judicial intervention if difficulties arise. Rule 58.01 governs production by parties, Rule 58.02 subpoenas non-parties, and RSMo 515.130 gives referees document-compulsion authority; the procedures and actors differ.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 275 impose la remise à l’expert des documents nécessaires et permet au juge d’en ordonner la production, avec des conséquences en cas de carence. Les Rules 58.01 et 61.01 prévoient respectivement la production et les sanctions en cas de non-respect. Le RSMo 510.030 prévoit la production sur ordonnance, sans sanction dans le texte fourni. Ces mécanismes ne sont pas spécifiques à l’expertise.
correspondences.note_en: Article 275 requires parties to provide necessary documents to the expert and permits an order compelling production, with consequences for noncompliance. Rules 58.01 and 61.01 address production and sanctions, respectively. RSMo 510.030 authorizes production by court order but states no sanction in the supplied text. None is expert-specific.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut ordonner la production de pièces de comparaison et faire composer des échantillons d’écriture. Rule 58.01 et RSMo 510.030 permettent d’ordonner la production et l’inspection de documents ou objets, mais ne réglementent pas spécifiquement les échantillons d’écriture ni la vérification graphologique.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may require comparison documents and dictated handwriting samples. Rule 58.01 and RSMo 510.030 authorize orders for production and inspection of documents or tangible things, but do not specifically regulate handwriting samples or judicial handwriting verification.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge conserve l’écrit contesté et les pièces de comparaison, ou en ordonne le dépôt au greffe. Les textes du Missouri permettent d’ordonner ou de demander la production et l’inspection de documents, mais ne prévoient pas ici leur dépôt au greffe pour vérification d’écriture.
correspondences.note_en: The judge retains the disputed writing and comparison materials or orders their filing with the clerk. Missouri provisions authorize court-ordered or requested production and inspection of documents, but do not provide for filing them with the clerk for handwriting verification.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut demander des explications et ordonner la production de documents, puis tirer des conséquences de l'abstention ou du refus. Les Rules 58.01 et 61.01 organisent la production et les sanctions, tandis que la Rule 62.01 permet au juge de diriger une conférence de gestion, mais aucune ne reprend exactement ce pouvoir général exercé d'office.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may request explanations, order production of documents, and draw consequences from noncompliance. Rules 58.01 and 61.01 address production and sanctions, while Rule 62.01 permits court-directed case management; none reproduces the same general sua sponte power.

correspondences.note_fr: Les héritiers doivent remettre les documents utiles, et le mandataire peut les convoquer pour les informer et les entendre. Les Rules 56.01 et 58.01 offrent des mécanismes de discovery et de production documentaire, mais sur demande procédurale et sans reprendre l’obligation successorale ni le pouvoir général de convocation.
correspondences.note_en: Heirs must provide useful documents, and the administrator may convene them for information and consultation. Rules 56.01 and 58.01 provide discovery and document-production mechanisms, but only through procedural requests and without reproducing the succession-specific duty or general power to convene heirs.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’instruction arbitrale, l’audition de personnes et la production forcée de pièces sous astreinte. Les Rules 56.01, 58.01 et 57.03 offrent des mécanismes judiciaires comparables de découverte, de production et de déposition; la Rule 61.01 prévoit des sanctions, mais dans un cadre et selon des effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs arbitral investigation, witness hearing, and compelled production subject to a coercive penalty. Rules 56.01, 58.01, and 57.03 provide comparable court-discovery, production, and deposition mechanisms; Rule 61.01 supplies enforcement sanctions, but in a different setting and with different effects.

norms.heading: Subpoena to Non-Party for Production of Documents and Things

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 58 — Production of Documents and Things and Entry Upon Land for Inspection and Other Purposes

norms.text:
(a) Scope. A party may serve a subpoena on a non-party to:

(1) Produce and permit inspection and copying of any designated documents, or

(2) Permit inspection, copying testing, or sampling of any tangible things that constitute or contain matters within the scope of Rule 56.01(b) and that are in the possession, custody or control of the non-party.
(3) Every such subpoena for document production and things shall:

(A) Be issued by the clerk of the court in which the civil action is pending;

(B) State the name of the court and they style of the civil action;

(C) State the name, address, and telephone number of all attorneys of record and self-represented parties.
(b) Time. A subpoena to a non-party shall be served not fewer than 10 days before the time specified for compliance.

(c) Notice to Parties. The party serving a subpoena on a non-party pursuant to Rule 58.02(a) shall provide a copy of the subpoena to every party as if it were a pleading. A party objecting to the subpoena may seek a protective order under Rule 56.01(c).
(d) Response. With the agreement of all parties, the non-party may be excused from appearance at the location specified for document production and may produce the subpoenaed items to the party responsible for issuance and service of the subpoena, who shall then offer to all other parties the opportunity to inspect or copy the subpoenaed items.
The party responsible for issuance and service of the subpoena is responsible for obtaining the agreement of all parties and advising the non-party in writing of the agreement, with a copy to all attorneys of record and self-represented parties. Absent such an agreement, the subpoenaed items shall only be produced at the place, date and time specified by the subpoena for all parties to inspect or copy.
Upon request by any party, the non-party shall also produce with the subpoenaed items a business records affidavit of the custodian of records.

(e) Protection of Non-Party.

(1) A party or attorney responsible for the issuance and service of a subpoena shall take reasonable steps to avoid imposing undue burden or expense on a non-party subject to the subpoena.
(2) A non-party commanded to produce and permit inspection and copying may serve the party who issued and served the subpoena with a written objection to inspection and copying of any or all of the designated items. The objection shall state specific reasons why the subpoena should be quashed or modified. The objection shall be served on all parties to the action within 10 days after service of the subpoena or before the time specified for compliance, whichever is earlier.
(3) If a timely and specific objection is made, the party who issued and served the subpoena shall not be entitled to inspect or copy the subpoenaed items except pursuant to an order of the court.

(f) Contempt. Any person who without adequate excuse fails to obey a subpoena served upon the person may be held in contempt of the court in which the civil action is pending.

Les règles du Missouri organisent la subpoena et la production par les non-parties, avec possibilité de contempt, mais ne détaillent pas toutes ces mesures de gestion documentaire.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may compel third parties to produce documents, under coercion, and prescribe preservation, inspection, copying, and return measures. Missouri rules provide subpoenas and production by non-parties, with possible contempt, but do not detail all of these document-management measures.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge de la mise en état dispose de pouvoirs généraux pour communiquer, obtenir et faire produire les pièces. Les règles du Missouri organisent la discovery et la production par les parties ou par subpoena, avec des conditions et techniques différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The juge de la mise en état has broad powers to obtain and compel production of documents. Missouri Rules 56.01 and 58.02, together with RSMo 510.030, address discovery and document production through party requests, court orders, and subpoenas, but under materially different mechanisms and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: Le magistrat peut ordonner d’office des mesures d’instruction et imposer, sous astreinte, la production de documents par une partie ou un tiers. Rule 56.01 organise la discovery, Rule 58.02 la production par un tiers et Rule 61.01 les conséquences du défaut, mais sans reprendre exactement le pouvoir d’office ni l’astreinte.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may order investigative measures sua sponte and compel a party or nonparty to produce documents subject to a penalty. Rule 56.01 governs discovery, Rule 58.02 nonparty production, and Rule 61.01 enforcement, but none exactly reproduces the sua-sponte power or French astreinte.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1469 permet d’obtenir judiciairement la production, par un tiers, d’un acte ou d’une pièce à la suite d’une invitation du tribunal arbitral. Les Rules 58.02 et 57.09 permettent la production de documents par subpoena contre un non-partie, mais ne prévoient ni le mécanisme arbitral ni la même procédure judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1469 permits court-ordered production by a non-party following an invitation from the arbitral tribunal. Rules 58.02 and 57.09 permit document production by subpoena from a non-party, but provide neither the arbitral mechanism nor the same court procedure.

norms.heading: Request for and Effect of Admissions

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 59 — Admission of Facts and of Genuineness of Documents

norms.text:
(a) Scope. After commencement of an action, a party may serve upon any other party no more than 25 written requests for the admission, without leave of court or stipulation of the parties, for purposes of the pending action only, of the truth of any matters within the scope of Rule 56.01(b) set forth in the request that relate to statements or opinions of fact or of the application of law to fact, including the genuineness or foundation of any documents described in the request.
However, the limitation on the number of requests for admission specified by this Rule 59.01 shall not apply to requests for admission regarding the genuineness or admissibility of documents.

(1) The request for admissions shall have included at the beginning of said request the following language in all capital letters, boldface type, and a character size that is as large as the largest character size of any other material in the request:
"A FAILURE TO TIMELY RESPOND TO REQUESTS FOR ADMISSIONS IN COMPLIANCE WITH RULE 59.01 SHALL RESULT IN EACH MATTER BEING ADMITTED BY YOU AND NOT SUBJECT TO FURTHER DISPUTE."

(2) Except in cases where the provisions of Chapter 517 apply, a failure to timely respond to requests for admissions in compliance with this Rule 59.01 shall result in each matter being admitted.
In cases where the provisions of Chapter 517 apply, upon a party's failure to timely respond to requests for admissions the court may, upon motion and reasonable notice to the parties, take such actions in regard to the failure to respond as are just, and among others the following:

(i) Grant a non-responding party additional time to respond;
(ii) Order no response be required;

(iii) Order the requests for admissions be revised, or reformatted and served again, or served again in a specific manner or place; or

(iv) Order any proper request for admission be deemed admitted in the pending action against the non-responding party.

(b) Effect of Admission. Any matter admitted under this Rule 59.01 is conclusively established unless the court on motion permits withdrawal or amendment of the admission.
Subject to the provisions of Rule 62.01 governing amendment of a pre-trial order, the court may permit withdrawal or amendment when the presentation of the merits of the action will be subserved thereby and the party who obtained the admission fails to satisfy the court that withdrawal or amendment will prejudice the party in maintaining the action or defense on the merits.
Any admission made by a party under this Rule 59.01 is for the purpose of the pending action only and is not an admission by the party for any other purpose nor may it be used against the party in any other proceeding.

(c) Issuance.

(1) Form. In consecutively numbered paragraphs, the request shall set forth each matter for which an admission is requested. Copies of documents about which admissions are requested shall be served with the request unless copies have already been furnished. The title shall identify the party to whom the request for admissions are directed and state the number of the set of requests directed to that party.
(2) When Requests May Be Served. Without leave of court, requests may be served on:

(A) A plaintiff after commencement of the action,

(B) A defendant or respondent upon the expiration of 30 days after the first event of the defendant entering an appearance or being served with process, and

(C) Any other party with or after the party was served with process, entered an appearance, or filed a pleading.
(3) Service. Copies of the requests shall be served on all parties not in default. The party issuing the requests shall also provide each responding party an electronic copy in a commonly used medium, such as a diskette, CD-ROM, or as an e-mail attachment, in a format that can be read by most commonly used word processing programs, such as Word for Windows or WordPerfect 5.x or higher. In addition to the information normally in a certificate of service, the certificate of service shall also state the:
(A) Name of each party who is to respond to the requests;

(B) Number of the set of requests; and

(C) Format of the electronic copy and the medium used to transmit the electronic copy to the responding party.

At the time of service, a certificate of service, but not the requests, shall be filed with the court as provided in Rule 59.01(d).
(d) Response. The requests shall be answered by each party to whom they are directed.

(1) When Response Is Due. Responses shall be served within 30 days after the service of the requests for admissions. A defendant or respondent, however, shall not be required to respond to requests for admissions before the expiration of 60 days after the earlier of the defendant:
(A) Entering an appearance, or

(B) Being served with process.

The court may allow a shorter or longer time.

(2) Form. The title of the response shall identify the responding party and the number of the set of the requests for admissions. The response shall quote each request, including its original paragraph number, and immediately thereunder specifically:
(A) Admit the matter;

(B) Deny the matter;

(C) Object to the matter and state each reason for the objection; or

(D) Set forth in detail the reasons why the responding party cannot truthfully admit or deny the matter.

A denial shall fairly meet the substance of the requested admission.

When good faith requires that a party qualify an answer or deny only a part of the matter of which an admission is requested, the party shall specify so much of it as true and qualify or deny the remainder.
A responding party may give lack of information or knowledge as a reason for failure to admit or deny if such party states that the party has made reasonable inquiry and the information known or readily obtainable by the party is insufficient to enable the party to admit or deny.

A party who considers that a matter of which an admission has been requested presents a genuine issue for trial may not, on that ground alone, object to the request; such party may deny the matter, subject to the provisions of Rule 61.01(c), or set forth reasons why the party cannot admit or deny it.
(3) Objections and Privileges. If an objection is asserted, then each reason for the objection shall be stated. If a failure to admit or deny a request is based on a privilege or the work product doctrine, then without revealing the protected information, the objecting party shall state information that will permit others to assess the applicability of the privilege or work product doctrine.
(4) Signing. The response shall be signed by the party or the party's attorney.

(5) Service. The party to whom the requests were directed shall serve a signed original of the response and objections, if any, on the party that issued the requests and a copy upon all parties not in default. The certificate of service shall state the name of the party who issued the requests and the number of the set of requests.
At the time of service, a certificate of service, but not the response, shall be filed with the court as provided in Rule 59.01(d).

(e) Filing Request and Responses. The request and response thereto shall not be filed with the court except upon court order or contemporaneously with a motion placing the request in issue. However, both when the request and the response are served the party serving them shall file with the court a certificate of service. Each party filing a certificate shall maintain a copy of the document that is the subject of the certificate until the case is finally disposed.
(f) Enforcement. The party who has requested the admissions may move to have determined the sufficiency of the answers or objections. Unless the court determines that an objection is proper, it shall order that an answer be served. If the court determines that an answer does not comply with the requirements of this Rule 59.01, it may order either that:
(1) The matter is admitted, or

(2) An amended answer be served.

The provisions of Rule 61.01(c) apply to the award of expenses incurred in relation to the motion.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 285 répartit la compétence pour la vérification incidente ou principale des écritures sous seing privé. Les règles 59.01 et 510.050 organisent les demandes d’admission de l’authenticité des documents, mais ne répartissent pas cette compétence entre juridictions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 285 allocates jurisdiction over incidental or principal verification of private writings. Rules 59.01 and 510.050 provide procedures for admitting the genuineness of documents, but do not allocate jurisdiction between courts.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge vérifie l’écriture ou la signature contestée, y compris électroniques, sauf inutilité. Les Rules 59.01 et RSMo 510.050 organisent surtout l’admission ou le refus de l’authenticité des documents, avec effet procédural, mais ne prévoient pas la vérification judiciaire de l’écriture elle-même.
correspondences.note_en: The court verifies disputed handwriting or signatures, including electronic ones, unless unnecessary. Rules 59.01 and RSMo 510.050 mainly provide for requests to admit or deny document genuineness and their procedural effects, but do not establish judicial handwriting verification itself.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque le défendeur reconnaît l'écriture, le juge en donne acte. La Rule 59.01 traite de l'admission de l'authenticité des documents et rend l'admission concluante, mais selon la procédure distincte des demandes d'admission.
correspondences.note_en: When the defendant acknowledges the handwriting, the judge records that acknowledgment. Rule 59.01 addresses admissions of document genuineness and makes them conclusive, but through the distinct requests-for-admission procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: Le déni ou la méconnaissance de l'écriture entraîne une procédure de vérification. La Rule 59.01 permet de nier l'authenticité d'un document dans le cadre de demandes d'admission, mais n'organise pas une vérification d'écriture comparable. La Rule 74.05, non retenue, concerne le défaut de plaider ou de se défendre.
correspondences.note_en: A denial or failure to recognize handwriting triggers a verification procedure. Rule 59.01 permits denial of a document’s genuineness through requests for admission, but does not establish comparable handwriting verification. Rule 74.05, not retained, concerns failure to plead or otherwise defend.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 299 organise l’examen judiciaire d’un écrit sous seing privé argué de faux en renvoyant aux articles 287 à 295. Le RSMo 510.060(3) prévoit la contestation et la preuve de l’authenticité d’un document, avec une éventuelle imputation des frais; la Rule 59.01 encadre les admissions relatives à l’authenticité, sans organiser l’incident de faux lui-même.
correspondences.note_en: Article 299 directs the court to examine a private writing alleged to be forged under Articles 287–295. RSMo 510.060(3) addresses denial and proof of a document’s genuineness, with possible costs, while Rule 59.01 governs admissions concerning genuineness but does not establish a forgery incident procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’absence du défendeur ou sa volonté d’utiliser la pièce entraîne la poursuite de la procédure de faux. Les Rules 59.01 et 61.01(c) concernent les admissions et les conséquences du défaut de réponse sur l’authenticité des documents; RSMo 517.131 prévoit, dans son champ propre, le jugement par défaut en cas de non-comparution.
correspondences.note_en: The defendant’s nonappearance or decision to use the document leads to continuation of the forgery procedure. Rules 59.01 and 61.01(c) address admissions and nonresponse concerning document genuineness; RSMo 517.131 provides, in its own setting, for default judgment after nonappearance.

norms.heading: Examination and Report

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 60 — Physical and Mental Examination of Persons

norms.text:
(a) Order for Examination.

(1) In an action in which the mental condition, physical condition, or blood relationship of a party, or of an agent or a person in the custody or under the legal control of a party, is in controversy, the court in which the action is pending may order the party

(i) to submit to physical, mental, or blood examinations by physicians or other appropriate licensed health care providers or
(ii) to produce for such examinations such party's agent or the person in such party's custody or legal control.

(2) In any action in which the vocational ability of a party, or of an agent or a person in the custody or under the legal control of a party, is in controversy, the court in which the action is pending may order the party
(i) to submit to evaluation by vocational rehabilitation professionals or

(ii) to produce for such evaluation such party's agent or the person in such party's custody or legal control.
(3) Any order under this Rule 60.01(a) may be made only on motion for good cause shown, upon notice to the person against whom the order is sought and to all other parties. Such order shall specify the time, place, manner, conditions, scope of, and identity of each person conducting the examination or evaluation. The court may, as a condition of its order, require the party requesting the order to reimburse the person who is the subject of the order for that person's reasonable round trip expenses in traveling more than sixty miles from the place of residence to the place of examination or evaluation.
(b) Report of Findings.
(1) If requested by the party against whom an order is made under Rule 60.01(a) or the person who is the subject of the order, the party obtaining the order shall deliver to the requesting person or party a copy of a detailed written report of the examiner or evaluator setting out the findings, including results of all tests made, diagnosis, and conclusions, together with like reports of all earlier examinations or evaluations of the same condition.
After delivery, the party obtaining the order shall be entitled upon request to receive from the party against whom the order is made a like report of any examination or evaluation, previously or thereafter made, of the same condition, unless, in the case of a report of examination or evaluation of a person not a party, the party shows an inability to obtain it. The court on motion shall make an order against a party requiring delivery of a report on such terms as are just; if an examiner or evaluator fails or refuses to make a report, the court may exclude the examiner's or evaluator's testimony if offered at the trial.
(2) By requesting and obtaining a report of the examination or evaluation so ordered or by taking the deposition of the examiner or evaluator, the person examined or evaluated waives any privilege the person may have in that action, or any other involving the same controversy, regarding the testimony of every other person who has examined or evaluated or may thereafter examine or evaluate the person in respect of the same mental condition, physical condition, vocational ability, or blood relationship.
(3) This Rule 60.01(b) applies to examinations made by agreement of the parties, unless the agreement expressly provides otherwise, and does not preclude discovery of a report of or the taking of a deposition of the examiner or evaluator in accordance with the provisions of any other rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article impose la remise d'un rapport écrit aux parties et attribue, dans une convention entre avocats, une valeur équivalente à celle d'un avis d'expert judiciaire. La Rule 60.01(b) prévoit la remise de rapports d'examen, y compris pour les examens convenus, et la Rule 68.01 ainsi que RSMo 452.390 organisent la remise de rapports, mais aucun ne confère exactement cette valeur probatoire à un rapport privé de technicien.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a written report to be delivered to the parties and gives a report under an agreement between lawyers the same value as a court-appointed expert opinion. Rule 60.01(b) covers reports, including agreed examinations, and Rule 68.01 and RSMo 452.390 govern report disclosure, but none gives precisely the same evidentiary status to a privately retained technician’s report.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut vérifier personnellement les faits litigieux, procéder à des constatations ou reconstitutions et se transporter sur les lieux. Les textes du Missouri permettent une expertise physique ou mentale ordonnée par le tribunal, mais non une vérification personnelle générale du juge.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may personally verify disputed facts, make observations or reconstructions, and visit the site. Missouri provisions authorize court-ordered physical or mental examinations, but not a general personal verification by the judge.

correspondences.note_fr: Si la vérification n'est pas immédiate, le juge en fixe le lieu, le jour et l'heure, et peut désigner un membre de la formation. Les règles du Missouri traitent du lieu des actes judiciaires et imposent que les ordonnances d'examen précisent notamment le temps et le lieu, sans prévoir cette désignation.
correspondences.note_en: If verification is not immediate, the judge sets its place, date, and time and may designate a member of the panel. Missouri rules address the place of judicial acts and require examination orders to specify time and place, but do not provide the same designation mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le technicien doit exécuter personnellement la mission en raison de sa qualification; pour une personne morale, les personnes physiques doivent être agréées. La Rule 60.01 exige que l’ordonnance précise l’identité de chaque personne conduisant l’examen, mais ne reprend ni l’obligation générale d’exécution personnelle ni le mécanisme applicable aux personnes morales.
correspondences.note_en: The technician must personally perform the assigned mission, and a legal entity must submit its responsible individuals for approval. Rule 60.01 requires the examination order to identify each person conducting it, but does not generally impose personal performance or regulate legal-entity technicians in the same way.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise toute mesure d’information sur la personnalité et les conditions de vie du mineur et de ses parents, notamment enquête éducative, examens médicaux et expertises psychologiques ou psychiatriques. Le RSMo 211.455 prévoit une enquête sociale et des évaluations, tandis que les autres textes concernent des enquêtes ou examens dans des cadres différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes inquiries into the personality and living conditions of the child and parents, including educational investigations, medical examinations, and psychological or psychiatric expertise. RSMo 211.455 provides a social investigation and evaluations; the other provisions address comparable inquiries or examinations in different procedural settings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1212 permet au juge des tutelles et au procureur de faire examiner certains majeurs par un médecin. Les textes du Missouri permettent au tribunal d’ordonner un examen physique ou mental lorsque l’état de la personne est en cause, mais exigent une motion, un motif valable et un avis, sans conférer ce pouvoir au procureur.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1212 allows the tutorship judge and prosecutor to obtain a medical examination of certain adults. Missouri permits court-ordered physical or mental examinations when a person’s condition is in controversy, but requires a motion, good cause, and notice, and does not grant the stated authority to a prosecutor.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose un certificat médical circonstancié décrivant l’altération, son évolution et ses effets sur la capacité civile, remis sous pli cacheté au juge ou au procureur. La Rule 60.01 prévoit des examens et rapports détaillés dans une action civile, mais ne prévoit ni ce certificat ni sa remise sous pli cacheté.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a detailed medical certificate addressing impairment, prognosis, and effects on civil capacity, delivered sealed to the judge or prosecutor. Rule 60.01 provides examinations and detailed reports in a civil action, but not this certificate or its sealed delivery.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise le juge à ordonner d’office ou sur demande toute mesure d’instruction, notamment une enquête sociale ou des constatations. RSMo 452.390 et 211.455 prévoient des enquêtes et rapports dans des procédures de garde ou de protection de l’enfance; Rule 60.01 vise plus spécifiquement les examens physiques ou mentaux.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the judge to order any investigative measure, including a social inquiry or findings by a person of the judge’s choice. RSMo 452.390 and 211.455 authorize investigations and reports in custody or child-protection proceedings, while Rule 60.01 more narrowly concerns physical or mental examinations.
